institution_zhou_enfeoffment_desc: Land is parcelled out to kin and retainers who hold full military and civil power in their fiefs.
institution_huaxia_tributary_system_desc: The Son of Heaven at the centre, the four quarters submitting: neighbours send envoys and tribute in return for investiture and trade. Required before accepting tributaries or waging tribute wars.
institution_zhou_forbid_private_wars_des: Lords may no longer wage war on their own; the right of conquest reverts to the crown.
institution_zhou_reduce_vassals_desc: Fiefs are dismantled into commanderies run by appointed officials instead of hereditary lords. If the vassals already hold their fiefs by hereditary right, this becomes an abolition of the domains, with far greater resistance and risk of rebellion.
institution_youmu_tribal_confederation_d: Tribes swear to a paramount chief; the confederation gathers on plunder and scatters on dispute.
institution_youmu_subject_register_desc: Settled subjects are enrolled in registers, giving the steppe realm a countable tax and manpower base.
institution_youmu_provincial_tax_farming: Tax districts are auctioned to merchant collectors: revenue spikes at once, and the provinces are squeezed raw.
institution_youmu_dual_administration_de: Steppe law governs the nomads and settled law the farmers: two parallel bureaucracies that never merge.
institution_culture_ranking_hint: Tiers use the highest advancement in each branch. Lowering one manually causes institutional regression and angers groups that lose established benefits.
institution_western_classical_city_repub: Assemblies and elected magistrates run the city: power is term-limited, collegial and checked.
institution_western_feudalization_desc: Offices become fiefs and fiefs become heritable: public authority fragments into layers of private homage.
institution_western_feudal_contract_desc: Homage runs both ways: the lord must respect chartered privileges, and breach entitles vassals to defy him.
institution_western_secular_estates_desc: Estates trade tax consent for a legislative voice, and secular orders begin to outweigh the church.
institution_western_centralized_monarchy: Standing armies, crown tax collectors and royal courts replace feudal middlemen: the king reaches every subject.
institution_western_clerical_supremacy_d: The church controls investiture, schooling and conscience; secular rulers must bow to it.
institution_western_theocratic_state_des: Crown and altar merge: the ruler governs by divine mandate and the clerical hierarchy is the civil service.
institution_arabic_tribal_shura_desc: Chieftains deliberate and acclaim a paramount leader; authority rests on clan consent, not office.
institution_arabic_caliphal_diwan_desc: Registries of people, pay and correspondence turn oral rule into filed administration.
institution_arabic_iqta_military_fiscal_: Tax districts replace salaries for commanders: the army pays itself, and stops asking the court's permission.
institution_arabic_sultanate_bureaucracy: A soldier-sultan holds real power, the caliph becomes symbolic, and the bureaucracy reorganizes around military merit.
institution_arabic_ulama_jurisprudence_d: Jurists control interpretation and the courts; the ruler's decrees need their sanction to be lawful.
institution_arabic_caliphal_theocracy_de: The sovereign heads the faith itself: decree and doctrine merge, and dissent becomes heresy.
institution_huaxia_prefecture_county_bur: The realm becomes uniform prefectures and counties run by assessed, rotated officials — rule by paperwork, not blood. Reached either by abolishing the fiefs outright or gradually through the Grace Edict.
institution_huaxia_examination_officiald: Office is won by written examination, opening the bureaucracy to commoners and narrowing hereditary privilege. Replaces the Recommendation System.
institution_huaxia_warlord_succession_de: Regional garrison commanders grow powerful enough to decide succession by force, unlocking the Rule of the Strongest succession law.
institution_huaxia_tactical_drilling_des: Standardized drill formations and battlefield doctrine improve every soldier's combat performance.
institution_huaxia_patriarchal_clan_desc: Rule rests on kinship and ritual: the sovereign heads the senior lineage. Under patriarchal custom, automatic appointments and faction leadership favor men.
institution_huaxia_well_field_desc: Fields are divided into public and private plots; households farm the common plot in lieu of tax.
institution_huaxia_land_equalization_des: Land and levies are assigned per registered adult, moving the tax base from lords to the state census. The state allots land per adult and restricts its accumulation.
institution_huaxia_salt_iron_monopoly_de: Salt, iron and liquor become state monopolies, doubling revenue without new taxes — and angering merchants.
institution_huaxia_military_garrison_des: Soldier-farmers serve in rotation from state garrisons, cutting costs and ending reliance on lords' retainers.
institution_arabic_caravan_trade_desc: Camel caravans link desert routes; tolls and markets become the treasury's mainstay.
institution_arabic_mamluk_corps_desc: Slave-soldiers form a standing elite loyal only to whoever pays them — until they decide to rule themselves.
institution_arabic_jizya_tax_desc: A per-head tax on non-adherents buys them autonomy and exemption from service.
institution_western_civic_legion_desc: Propertied citizens arm themselves and fight in formation; service and franchise reinforce each other.
institution_western_roman_law_desc: Codified statute plus juristic commentary gives contract, property and litigation rules that can be cited.
institution_western_manorial_economy_des: Self-sufficient manors bind serfs to the lord's land and the lord's court.
institution_western_burgher_charters_des: Towns buy charters of self-rule; guilds and councils carve an enclave out of feudal jurisdiction.
institution_youmu_khuriltai_election_des: Princes and nobles convene to raise a khan: succession turns on acclamation and strength, not birth order.
institution_youmu_decimal_army_desc: The whole people is organized in tens, hundreds and thousands, dissolving old tribal lines into chains of command.
institution_youmu_steppe_law_desc: A written khanal code overrides tribal custom: the khan's will finally outranks tradition.
institution_youmu_horse_archer_doctrine_: Light horse archery and feigned retreat become doctrine, trading mass for decisive mobility over settled armies.
institution_youmu_post_relay_network_des: Relay stations span the realm; edicts and intelligence travel at the speed of fresh horses.
institution_youmu_provincial_system_desc: Branch secretariats administer conquered farmland through a permanent provincial hierarchy — the steppe empire's answer to settling down.

institution_huaxia_two_tax_law_desc: Levies shift from personal labor obligations to twice-yearly assessments of land and property, moving the tax base from bodies to wealth. Replaces the Equal-Field system.
institution_huaxia_single_whip_reform_de: Land tax, labor service and miscellaneous levies are consolidated into a single silver payment, simplifying accounts while forcing households into the cash economy.
institution_huaxia_abolish_well_field_de: The well-field system is abolished: private fields are recognized, taxed by area, and may be bought and sold. Feudal regimes have no landlord class, so the land market only truly functions after the switch to the Code-and-Statute regime.
institution_huaxia_merit_ranks_desc: Ranks are granted for battlefield merit, letting commoners rise into the nobility and ending the hereditary lords' monopoly on arms.
institution_huaxia_recommendation_desc: Local officials recommend the filial and talented for office, giving the court control of appointments — though family standing and favoritism creep in.
institution_huaxia_constitutional_prepar: Constitutional government is prepared: provinces seat consultative assemblies and the court an advisory council where gentry and merchants debate state affairs. This is Huaxia's administrative basis for constitutional monarchy; requires the Prefecture-County Bureaucracy and the Single Whip Reform.
institution_resistance_reason_constituti: Gentry and merchants debating policy in the assemblies erodes absolute rule by the throne and its officials
institution_huaxia_recruited_army_desc: A treasury-funded professional army replaces rotating militia service, improving reliability while increasing military costs and commanders' influence.
institution_western_great_charter_desc: The ruler accepts written limits on taxation, justice and the punishment of vassals, turning feudal custom into enforceable political privilege.
institution_western_parliamentary_taxati: The estates trade tax consent for deliberation and oversight, converting urban wealth into durable political representation.
institution_western_reformation_desc: Local churches and secular rulers challenge universal clerical authority, redrawing the boundaries of faith, church property and political loyalty.
institution_arabic_bayt_al_mal_desc: Tribute, booty and stipends are registered and distributed through a central treasury, replacing ad hoc tribal division with permanent finance.
institution_arabic_waqf_endowment_desc: Land and income are permanently endowed for worship, education and relief, stabilizing social provision while locking revenue into religious property.
institution_arabic_madrasa_network_desc: Endowments support colleges across the realm, standardizing legal education and supplying trained jurists and administrators.
institution_youmu_ulus_appanage_desc: People, pasture and revenue are granted to royal princes in return for loyalty in conquest, giving those princes a hereditary power base.
institution_youmu_keshig_guard_desc: Sons of tribal nobles form the khan's household guard: an elite army, a school for officials and a network of political hostages.
institution_youmu_religious_tolerance_de: Conquered peoples keep their faith and clergy, trading religious autonomy for taxes, expertise and imperial loyalty.

parliament_how_body:
[Seats] Parliament has {0} seats, divided among factions by central share using the largest-remainder method. Banned factions get no seats.
[Members] Each faction sends its own adult members, ranked by: holding office first, then performance, then renown. The emperor cannot sit in parliament. Seats a faction cannot fill stay vacant.
[Term] A general election is held every {1} years. When a member dies, leaves the empire or changes faction, their faction fills the seat in a by-election.
[Powers] Taxes cannot change unless pro-constitution members hold a majority. The emperor still reigns by succession law, no powerful minister arises while parliament sits, and the old cabinet is dissolved.
parliament_responsible_government_body: [Responsible government] Only the government side can start and advance faction claims. In a majority or minority government that is the PM's faction; in a coalition government it is every pro-constitution faction in the coalition. Claims advance faster when the government holds a majority.

Orange: anti-constitution

parliament_politics_body:
[Seats] Set by the order of magnitude of the population: 9 seats at 100 people, plus 6 for every tenfold increase (21 at 10,000, 33 at 1 million), up to 45. Takes effect at the next election.
[Forming a government] A party with a majority governs alone. Otherwise the largest party (then the second largest) courts the parties closest to it in ideology until it has a majority, forming a coalition; parties too far apart will not join. If talks fail, a minority government is formed.
[Cabinet] Under responsible government, ministries are divided among the governing parties by their seats, and each party picks its own ministers.
[No confidence] A minority government, rifts in the coalition, ministers accused of crimes, public unrest and an empty treasury all invite the opposition to call a vote of no confidence. If it passes, a new majority coalition takes over if one can be formed; otherwise parliament is dissolved for an early election.
[Agenda] The governing party pushes to change one constitutional clause at a time and needs enough votes to amend the constitution; without them it stalls at the second reading. After a change of government, the new government keeps the agenda if it agrees, otherwise drops it.

local_politics_help_body:
In electoral states (parties legal, a parliament, multiple parties), each province has its own party support based on its own voters. Halfway through each parliamentary term, local elections are held: the party with the most votes governs the province and one of its local members becomes governor.
Provinces governed by the coalition get +3 city loyalty. Provinces held by the opposition resist the center: -5 city loyalty, and the government agenda slows in proportion to the population they control (up to 40% slower).
If the opposition holds over 60% of the provinces in two local elections in a row, a unitary state is forced to amend its constitution and become federal. The capital province is run directly by the center and holds no local elections.

empirecraft_law_no_commoners_description: Each month, surplus ordinary residents are folded into population data (head counts grouped by class, culture and ideology). Only notable people (rulers, city lords, officials, nobles, landlords, party members) stay as units, cutting unit counts for much higher frame rates. When an office or city lordship is vacant, someone is raised from the population on the spot, so the total population stays the same. Production and construction are settled automatically from population data. Armies work like CK3 levies: in peacetime each city keeps a single general; when war breaks out, soldiers are raised on the spot from the population up to the city's troop limit and disbanded back into it when the war ends. Folded population grows through births and deaths: more food surplus means more births, prosperity lowers deaths but also birth rates, and famine and war raise deaths. How many people a city holds depends on its houses and other buildings. The population also produces by employment: peasants grow food, workers earn gold and speed up construction, merchants and citizens earn gold, and everyone eats one food per year. Turning this off freezes the folded population; it does not turn back into units.
